decisions.issues: Clean. Standing ranks of bare-chested nobles in mundus and shoulder cloths, brass open-wick lamps doubled in the polished floor, carved pillars, open outer doorway with a silver sheet of rain, sanctum shown only as gold fragments. No painted text. Captions fit in the dark ceiling and pillar-capital band across the top and on the low-detail floor at lower right.

Only candidate v01 fails the beat and the setting. (1) The script's single gap in the front rank is not shown: the nobles are bunched into left and right groups around a huge open floor full of reflections, which reads as the aisle (the aisle the king later walks in 1.5), not one empty place in a rank with a single lamp's reflection. (2) The foreground figure at lower right reads as a woman (jewelled ornament in the hair bun, drop earrings, saree-like red-bordered drape). That clashes with an all-male rank and with the Padmini caption, since Padmini is meant to be absent. (3) The sanctum doors show a whole standing golden idol, which breaks 'the god is never shown whole' and contradicts the reclining Padmanabha in fragments on page 2. Note for the page: the nobles stand in 1.1 and 1.2 but sit in 1.3 to 1.5.
decisions.correction: Every figure is a Nair nobleman: men only, with topknots or front tufts and moustaches or grey stubble, no jewelled hair ornaments, no drop earrings and no saree-like drapes, so that no figure can be read as a woman. Make the gap the subject: the front rank stands as one straight shoulder-to-shoulder line of men across the middle of the frame, seen from behind and a little above, and exactly one person-width space in that line stands empty, bare polished stone with a single lamp's flame reflected in it. The floor beyond the line is darker and less mirror-bright, so that one reflection reads clearly and the space does not look like an open aisle. At the far end the sanctum doors show only fragments of gold and shadow, never a whole standing idol or any complete figure of the god. Keep the rain-silvered outer doorway at upper left, the carved granite pillars, the brass open-wick lamps and the warm night light, and leave the dark upper wall and pillar area clear for two captions.

decisions.issues: Only candidate v01 fails. The two nobles beside Nagoji are near-copies of him: thick curled moustaches, grey at the temples, curly topknots and gold ear studs. That breaks 'draw each named person once, with no doubles', and the reader cannot tell which man is Nagoji. The beat is also wrong: the two nobles sit in the same row as Nagoji, not the rank ahead, and all three, Nagoji included, look back over their shoulders at the viewer instead of the nobles glancing sidelong at him. Nagoji himself (curly hair up with grey temples, moustache, clean chin, ear stud, silver chain, cream mundu and shoulder cloth) and the setting (rain doorway, lamps, polished floor) are good.
decisions.correction: Only Nagoji may have a thick curled moustache, grey at the temples, curly hair in a topknot and a gold ear stud: draw him exactly once, and make every other man clearly different. Stage it from in front of the back rows, looking toward the rear of the hall, with the open outer doorway and its silver monsoon rain behind him. Nagoji sits at the back among the lesser officers, facing the viewer in three-quarter view, face composed and eyes forward: Kerala topknot tied on the crown with grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and jaw, a tiny flush gold stud on the earlobe, the silver chain of office plainly visible across his bare chest, cream mundu and shoulder cloth. In the foreground is the rank ahead of him, seen from behind and a little to the side. In that rank, exactly two nobles turn their heads back over their shoulders and glance sidelong at Nagoji, with their eyes on him, not on the viewer. One is a heavy older man with a shaven head, a small front tuft and heavy gold ear-rings; the other is a thin younger man with his hair loose and no moustache. Everyone else faces forward. Keep the seated rows on the polished, lamp-reflecting floor, the brass open-wick lamps and the dark carved pillars, and leave the dark ceiling and upper pillar area clear for two captions.

decisions.issues: Acceptable with minor deviations. The attendant still has the conch at his lips rather than lowering it; the beat (conch sounded, herald announcing) still reads. Both are correctly not priests: a young slight attendant in a short mundu with a crown knot, and a middle-aged herald in a white mundu with a staff, chin raised, mouth open. The nobles in front are seated, while 1.1 and 1.2 show them standing. A small seated statue in a side doorway at right reads as a carving, not the god. No painted text. The three herald balloons fit in the rain doorway at upper left and the dark ceiling band above the herald, clear of faces.

Acceptable. Varma matches the aged dedication sheet: grey hair drawn back into a low knot, moustache, bare torso with the sacred thread, plain white mundu, no jewels or headwear. He enters from the rain-filled far doorway, the silk-wrapped hilt and flame-lit blade held across his body, and every noble's head is turned toward him. Minor issues: he grips the hilt in his right hand with the blade resting on his left palm, rather than lying flat across both palms; the mundu has a thin gold hem border; the nobles are seated, while 1.1 has them standing. No painted text. The two captions fit in the dark carved pillar areas at the top, to the left and right of the doorway, clear of faces.

v01 shows an EMPTY mandapa: none of the silent ranks of nobles the script calls for, so it contradicts page 1 (1.5 has the hall packed on both sides) and 2.4, where the nobles stand behind him. Varma is a large foreground figure, not small between the ranks. He grips a dark scabbarded sword in his fists, but 1.5 and 2.5 show a bare steel blade with a red silk-wrapped hilt resting flat across his palms. A small pearl earring shows at his ear, though the bible says no jewels. What works: the grey low knot, the sacred thread, the reflecting floor, the lamps, the priests at the far end and the rain through the outer doorway.
decisions.correction: Keep the low camera on the polished, reflecting granite floor, the receding carved granite pillars and brass lamp stands, the open outer doorway at left showing monsoon rain, the row of chanting priests on the low granite platform before the gold sanctum doors (chief priest in the centre facing us), and Varma seen from behind with his grey low knot, bare back, sacred thread and plain white mundu. Fix three things. (1) The hall is NOT empty: line both sides of the aisle with dense, silent ranks of bare-chested nobles in white mundus and shoulder cloths, seated and standing as on the previous page, leaving only a narrow open aisle of floor down the middle. (2) Varma must read small and alone between those ranks: place him in the middle distance, walking away from the camera down the empty aisle, no more than about a third of the frame height, not a large foreground figure. (3) He carries the same bare sword as on page 1: a naked steel blade with a red silk-wrapped hilt, resting flat across both upturned open palms held before him, with no scabbard and no fists gripping it. Varma wears no earring and no jewel of any kind. Keep the upper quarter of the frame (dark ceiling beams and shadowed pillar tops) free of heads and hands for two captions.

decisions.issues: Continuity break: Varma stands at the threshold with both arms hanging at his sides and his hands visibly empty. He carries the sword in 2.1 and lays it down in 2.5, so it cannot vanish here. Everything else works: the back view, grey low knot, sacred thread, plain mundu, the gold doors, the reverent fragments of the reclining god and serpent hoods with no face shown, the lamps and the reflecting floor.
decisions.correction: Keep everything that works: Varma from behind at the sanctum threshold, dwarfed by the gold door leaves, with his grey low knot, bare back with the sacred thread and plain white mundu; the reverent fragments of Lord Padmanabha through the doors (rising serpent hoods, a vast resting hand, gold ornament, no face); the brass lamps, the reflecting granite floor and the rain glimpsed through a far doorway at left. Fix the missing prop: Varma still carries the dedication sword, and his hands must NOT hang empty at his sides. His elbows are bent forward and he holds the bare sword flat across both upturned palms in front of his waist, so that from behind the naked steel blade tip shows past one hip and the red silk-wrapped hilt shows past the other, the blade level with the floor. Keep the upper-left area of shadowed pillars and ceiling clear of figures for one caption.

decisions.issues: Continuity break: Varma kneels with both palms flat on the floor and no sword anywhere, yet in the very next panel (2.5) his hands lower the sword to the stone. A tiny ear stud shows on his ear, though the bible says no jewels. Otherwise strong: the bowed aged face with moustache, the grey low knot, the sacred thread, the plain mundu, the still nobles behind, the bending lamp flame in the foreground, and dark ceiling space for the caption.
decisions.correction: Keep the kneeling figure on the reflecting stone before the threshold, the bowed head with the grey low knot, the aged varma-v1 face with thick moustache, the bare torso with the sacred thread, the plain white mundu, the still nobles standing behind at left, the near-foreground brass lamp with its bending flame, and the dark ceiling space at upper centre for the caption. Fix the missing prop: his hands are NOT flat on the floor and NOT empty. He kneels with his head bowed, holding the bare sword flat across both upturned open palms at knee height in front of him: naked steel blade pointing toward the sanctum, red silk-wrapped hilt nearest himself, not yet laid down (the next panel lays it on the stone). Varma wears no ear stud, earring or jewel of any kind.

decisions.issues: The framing is a medium shot of the whole kneeling figure, wider than the scripted tight strip on the hands. His moustache reads thinner and greyer than in 2.4. Accepted because the beat is clear: his hands lower a bare steel blade, point toward the sanctum, with a red silk-wrapped hilt that matches 1.5. The grey low knot, sacred thread, plain mundu and setting all match. Captions can sit over the shadowed pillars along the top or on the floor at lower left without touching his face, his hands or the sword.

Minor: a tiny gold speck just under the nose tip, at the top of the moustache (about 5 px at full size). It reads as a highlight at print size, but paint it out if it shows as a nose ornament. The mundu has gold kasavu borders rather than plain white, which matches the page 2 frames. Otherwise this is the aged varma-v1 face: grey hair in a low knot at the nape, sacred thread, bare torso, kneeling and lit gold from the sanctum, with rain in the outer doorway. There is no painted text, and the dark ceiling at top left and centre gives room for both balloons.

Clean. The wide shot is taken over the seated nobles' heads. Varma kneels small and bright at the far end, seen from behind, with a grey low knot, the sacred thread and a white mundu. The dark ceiling band above the sanctum and the upper pillars leaves room for the two balloons to run back toward the viewer.

Clean. Only the central chief priest carries the temple-priest sheet face; the other chanting priests have moustaches or beards and read as different men. In the foreground, the old noble has wet eyes and parted lips, with his hands joined in prayer, and the hands are sound. Both captions fit at the top corners, over the rain doorway on the left and the lamp tops on the right, clear of the raised hands.

Minor: Nagoji's jaw has light stubble shading, but there is no beard, and the curled moustache, small flush gold stud, topknot and grey temple are all correct. The silver chain of office shows clearly across his back. The chief's tuft sits at the crown rather than the front. The chief is heavy-set and shaven, with heavy gold ear-rings, a red-bordered shoulder cloth and grey stubble, and he leans right with a cupped hand toward the young, loose-haired neighbour. The balloon can sit in the upper band of pillars between Nagoji and the chief.

v01 misses the script beat and breaks continuity with 3.4. Nagoji's full face fills the left half instead of only his shoulder and chain at the left edge. The young neighbour is missing, so the chief whispers to Nagoji. Both men are seated, although they stand in 3.4. The silver chain of office is not visible.
decisions.correction: Composition correction: this is a closer two-shot of the whispering chief and his young neighbour, not of Nagoji. Do not show Nagoji's face. Show only a narrow sliver of his bare shoulder with the silver chain of office lying across it, cut off by the LEFT edge of the frame and filling no more than one tenth of the width. Centre-left is the heavy-set older chief (shaven head with a small tuft at the FRONT, heavy gold hoop ear-rings, red-bordered shoulder cloth, grey stubble, no thick moustache). He still leans to the right toward his neighbour, one hand cupped beside his mouth, eyes wide. On the right is the neighbour, younger and thin, with loose curly black hair and a plain cream shoulder cloth. His face is turned three-quarter toward the viewer and his lips twitch, pressed together and not smiling. All three men are STANDING side by side at the back of the hall facing the sanctum, exactly as in panel 3.4, never seated. Keep the same mandapa: carved granite pillars, brass open-wick lamps, the wet granite floor reflecting the flames and the rain-filled outer doorway at upper left. Keep the dark upper band above their heads clear for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Clean. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, receding hair, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus, hands sound. He stands among the bowed rows with the sanctum behind him at right, and his eyes are on the rows. A noble at right lifts his chin, which fits the script's 'a lifted chin there'. The open outer doorway shows rain, as the setting requires. The caption fits the dark pillar and ceiling area in the upper middle. Minor: the nobles here are bowed low on the floor, while in 4.3 they sit and in 4.5 they stand.

Acceptable. Nagoji shows the Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a small flush gold ear stud, a silver chain, a bare chest with shoulder cloth and no forehead marks. His chin reads clean-shaven: there is only the faint ink hatching of the house style, no beard. He looks aside toward the sanctum side. Minor: the lamplight is more even across his face than the 'half his face' the script asks for, and the shoulder cloth has a gold stripe. Both captions fit in the dark carved ceiling area at the upper right (about x 0.6 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.22) without touching his face.

Acceptable, with minor issues. Varma, aged varma-v1, is rising from one knee with a hand on his knee: grey low knot, moustache, sacred thread, no jewels. The young attendant has a small knot and steps in holding a bundle of thin ribs. Nobles on both sides whisper behind raised hands. Minor: (1) Varma's and the attendant's mundus have a thin gold border rather than plain white, though the neighbouring ch28 frames draw Varma the same way. (2) The sword on the stone is drawn as an ornate gold sheathed sword, not the bare blade with a red silk hilt from 2.5, and it lies behind him to the left rather than clearly at the sanctum threshold. (3) The broom ribs are pale straw here and darker brown in 4.4 and 4.5. The caption fits the upper middle among the dark pillar tops.

The only candidate, v01, fails the principal's identity: the king receiving the broom has NO moustache, a clean upper lip and a different face, so he does not read as varma-v1. Every neighbouring panel gives Varma his thick curled moustache. The panel prompt attaches no reference sheet, which is likely why the face drifted. Also, the attendant wears a long gold-bordered mundu with a shoulder cloth instead of a plain short mundu with a bare chest, and the frame is a medium shot on Varma's face, not a tight inset on the hand-off. The broom itself is good: coir-bound ribs, no pole, ragged tips, hands sound.
decisions.correction: Keep the hand-off of the coir-bound bundle of thin brown coconut-leaf ribs (no wooden pole, tips worn ragged) against the dark lamplit stone floor, but make it a true tight inset: frame at chest height and below so that NO face is in the picture. Show only the attendant's slim young bare forearms and hands reaching in from the left and the king's older, broader hands and forearms closing on the bundle from the right, with the white sacred thread visible across the king's bare chest and the top of his plain white mundu at the waist. If any part of the king's face does enter the frame, it must be the varma-v1 face from his attached sheet, aged, with his thick curled moustache under the nose and grey hair in a low knot at the back of the head, never a clean-shaven upper lip. The attendant is bare-chested in a plain short white mundu with no gold border and no shoulder cloth.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. Aged Varma kneels low before the golden sanctum doors, sweeping scattered flower petals with a short handleless rib broom: moustache, grey low knot, sacred thread, white mundu, hands sound. In the background the nobles stand frozen with their hands dropped and clasped and their mouths closed. Rain shows through the outer doorway. The frame is the required 3:1 strip, and the faces sit in the middle band. Minor: he is down on both knees rather than one, and his mundu has the thin gold border used throughout the chapter. The caption fits the dark ceiling and pillar tops in the upper middle (about x 0.42 to 0.6, y 0.02 to 0.18).

Minor only: Varma is in the middle distance, not the very small far figure the script asks for, and the high angle is moderate. Grey low knot, sacred thread, moustache, no jewels, short coconut-rib broom held mid-stroke, nobles at the edges, rain on the grove past the outer wall. The upper frame is busy with pillars, so both captions belong on the clear lamplit floor in the lower centre (x 0.25-0.80, y 0.65-0.95), which has no faces.

Minor: the chief has a short grey beard rather than stubble, and his look is a troubled hand-to-chin frown, which still reads as the knowing look gone. Varma kneels with the short broom, has a grey low knot and sacred thread, and wears no jewels. The sanctum shows only gold fragments, with no whole idol. The caption can sit in the dark low-detail area at top centre (x 0.48-0.73, y 0.0-0.13).

Minor: the broom here is a longer bundle than the short broom in panels 1-2, though it is still handleless coconut ribs. A soft gold idol-like shape shows through the sanctum door, but it is blurred, partial and half hidden by the attendant, so it reads as fragments of gold. Varma's mundu is dusty and his hands are ash-grey. He has a grey low knot at the nape and the sacred thread. The attendant is young and slight, with a short mundu and a small top knot. No lettering is needed.

None significant. Varma has turned to the assembly and looks toward the viewer from Nagoji's point of view. He has a grey low knot, the sacred thread and a dust-marked mundu, and wears no jewels. Nagoji is not drawn. The long caption fits in the dark empty ceiling at top right (x 0.55-0.88, y 0.0-0.18).

Minor: several chanting priests stand upright beside Varma, which softens 'the one head not bowed', though he is still the central, framed figure. The sword lies beside rather than directly behind his feet. The bowing chief shows his shaven head and red-bordered cloth but no visible gold ear-rings. Only the lamp-bearing chief priest has the temple-priest face, so there are no doubles. Lettering space is tight. Put the PRIESTS balloon over the rain at top left (x 0.04-0.14, y 0.0-0.15), with its tail to the lamp-bearing chief priest. Put the captions over the anonymous bowed backs in the bottom-left and bottom-right corners (y 0.85-1.0), clear of the chief, Varma and the sword.

Clean. Revathi matches her sheet and bible row (indigo and gold sari, grey streak, jasmine braid, coin necklace, tali on yellow thread, armlets, sandalwood line). Nagoji in the doorway matches (white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain, sword, grey topknot, curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud). Banner is plain red with a silver conch and no lettering. Open sky at upper centre takes both captions.

Minor: Revathi is seen from behind with her head in slight profile to frame right, so whether she faces the banner or him is a little ambiguous. Nagoji's hair hangs looser than in 6.1 and his sword is not visible. His face matches: clean chin, curled moustache, grey temples, small gold stud. Open sky upper middle and right, plus open flagstones, give room for three balloons.

Minor: up close there is faint mottled shading on the jaw, but it reads as clean-shaven at panel size. The banner hangs straight down from a crossbar instead of flying as in the other panels. Otherwise good: set jaw, diagonal shadow across the coat, grey topknot, tiny flush gold stud, uniform and chain. Sky between his head and the banner leaves room for the two off-panel balloons; tails point to the right edge, where he is looking.

v01 shows a second figure at frame right: a man in a cream kurta and shoulder cloth with a maroon sash and sword, short loose hair with no topknot, and a stubbled beard. If he is meant to be Nagoji, his costume and beard are wrong, and the prompt says Nagoji is off-panel. Otherwise he is a stray bystander. Revathi's grey threading is also barely visible. Her weary turn of the head, costume and the courtyard are otherwise good.
decisions.correction: Draw Revathi Bayi ALONE: no other person anywhere in the frame, with no man, guard or figure in the background, in a doorway or at the frame edge. Nagoji stands off-panel to frame right and must not appear at all. Frame her from the waist up or closer, at frame left or centre-left. Her body stays angled toward the gatehouse, and only her head turns over her shoulder toward frame right, where he is. Her face is weary and drained, with no anger, and her eyes are level. Keep what worked in the last attempt: deep indigo sari with gold zari, long braid with jasmine, flat-coin necklace with the tali on its yellow thread, gold armlets and bangles, bell earrings, sandalwood line at the hairline, early-evening gold light, laterite courtyard walls and the red banner with a silver conch above the tiled gatehouse. Make the grey threading in her black hair clearly visible as a grey streak at the temple, matching the earlier panels. Leave open, low-detail evening sky across the upper middle and upper right of the frame for three short speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Clean. Close on Revathi with a startled, newly seeing look toward Nagoji at frame right. All her bible details are present, including visible grey threading. Nagoji in the background matches (white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain, grey topknot, curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud). He is drawn sharp, not soft, which is acceptable. Nagoji is visible, so the tail for his 'off' line goes to his mouth. Sky across the top leaves room for three balloons.

Clean. Wide two-shot across a long stretch of flagstone in the fort courtyard. The tiled gatehouse and the red conch banner are in place, in low gold evening light. Nagoji is in the white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain and boots, with a grey-streaked topknot, no turban, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small gold stud. Revathi is in the indigo-and-gold sari with the jasmine braid, grey threading, tali pendant, gold armlets and sandalwood line. Brass oil lamps have open flames. There is open sky in the upper centre for both balloons.

Acceptable. Revathi turns a step toward the open gate with her face in profile against the sunset. The courtyard, gatehouse, conch banner and lighting match panel 1. One small oddity: her tali-style pendant hangs down her back, not her front. It does not read as an error at panel size. The sky upper right, between her head and the flag, holds both balloons.

Acceptable. Revathi turns back over her shoulder toward the viewer and Nagoji, who is off-panel. The courtyard and gatehouse match the page. Her grey threading, jasmine braid, armlets, bangles and sandalwood line are correct, and her hand is sound. Again the pendant thread falls at her back (minor). There is sky upper right for her two balloons. Nagoji's balloon tails off the right edge, where he stood in panel 1.

Clean. Tight on Revathi with the flat-coin necklace, tali on its yellow thread, jhumkas, jasmine braid, grey threading, sandalwood line and gold armlets. The same gatehouse and banner sit at sunset behind her. The panel on the gatepost is a blank carved relief, not text. There is sky in the upper centre and upper right for both balloons.

Clean. Full-width final beat: Revathi walks out through the open gate into the low gold evening, small, with her back turned. Nagoji stands still in the near foreground, in the white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain and sword, with a grey-streaked topknot, no turban, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small gold stud. The conch banner flies above the gate. Upper-centre sky takes her two balloons trailing back toward him, and the open flagstones low in the centre take his caption.

Clean. Ramayyan matches his sheet: receding curly hair, thin features, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus at his elbow. The commissioner wears a bag-wig, lace stock and dark cuffed coat, signs with a quill, and his tricorn is on the table. The soldiers wear blue coats, the treaty sheet is blank and there is no lettering. Caption space is fairly tight: use the roof and sky band along the top, between the soldiers' heads, plus the plain tablecloth at the front if needed.

Acceptable. Nagoji: white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain, topknot with grey at the temples, curled moustache, clean chin and a small gold bead stud. Varma: aged face, grey low knot, shoulder cloth and sacred thread. Minor: Varma's mundu has a thin gold border instead of plain white, which is consistent with 8.3 and 8.4. There is a large clear night sky for the caption.

Acceptable. Varma is seen from behind at the wet parapet, looking out at the dark. He has a grey low knot and moustache, and the sacred thread shows across his back. The setting matches 8.2. Minor continuity point: the shoulder cloth from 8.2 is gone and he is bare-torsoed here, which fits the bible row and 8.4 and 8.5. There is wide sky above for both balloons.

Acceptable. Varma has turned from the parapet, his head turned toward the off-panel Nagoji. He has the aged face, grey low knot, sacred thread, no jewels and the same mundu as 8.2 and 8.3. Minor: the script's plain shoulder cloth is absent, consistent with 8.3 and 8.5. He has a white and red namam on his forehead, which matches his face-study sheet and is not banned for Varma. His hands are behind his back. The upper-right sky is clear for the balloon.

v01 fails Nagoji's chapter look and breaks continuity with 8.2 on the same page. He has no grey at the temples (the hair is all black), and the hair falls in long loose curls to the shoulders with only a small knot on top. The chin and jaw show visible grey stubble shading, not a clean-shaven chin. His body is also turned away from Varma, looking back over his shoulder, instead of facing him. The over-the-shoulder framing, white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain, ear stud, Varma's grey low knot and sacred thread, and the night rampart all work.
decisions.correction: Keep the over-the-shoulder composition, the night rampart with distant fort lamps and camp lights, and Varma's grey low knot, bare shoulder and sacred thread at the right edge. Fix Nagoji to match the previous panel: gather his hair up into a neat Kerala topknot on the crown with clear grey streaks at both temples, with no long loose curls hanging to his shoulders. Shave his chin and jaw completely smooth, with no stubble, stipple or shadow. Keep the thick curled moustache and the tiny flush gold stud on the earlobe. Turn his body toward Varma in three-quarter front view so he faces him directly, not turned away and glancing back over his shoulder. Keep his face still and unreadable. Show the white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and the silver chain over the coat. Keep the upper-left and upper-centre night sky empty for three speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only: Varma has a small Vaishnavite forehead mark and a pin-point ear stud (the dedication look says no jewels), and his shoulder cloth has a gold border rather than plain. Otherwise on beat: over-the-shoulder back view, grey low knot, sacred thread, wet parapet at night, distant fort lamps, road and camp cookfires, open-wick brass lamp. No painted text. Large clear dark sky upper right and centre for the three balloons.

Wrong framing: the script calls for a tight insert on his hands gripping the parapet, knuckles pale on wet stone. v01 is a medium over-the-shoulder shot of the whole leaning figure and landscape that largely repeats 9.1, so the beat is lost. Hands, setting and Varma's look are otherwise fine.
decisions.correction: Frame this as a tight close-up insert of the hands only: Varma's two aged, veined hands clenched on the top edge of the wet dark stone parapet, filling the lower two-thirds of the frame, knuckles pale and tendons standing out, with at most the forearms coming in from the frame edge. Show no face, head, back or full figure, and do not repeat the previous panel's over-the-shoulder view of the landscape. No rings or bracelets on his hands. Keep the night-after-rain light: rain beading on the dressed stone with warm glints from a small brass open-wick oil lamp, and a dark blue night beyond the parapet edge in the upper third, left plain and low-detail for the two balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor: Varma's low knot is dark with grey streaks rather than fully grey as in 9.1 and 9.4. Otherwise on beat: close night face with a tear, sacred thread, plain shoulder cloth, wet parapet and camp lights. The memory bleeds in at the upper left as a ragged warm stain, not a framed flashback: young laughing Savitri, head thrown back, in a cream cloth with a red-and-gold border, gold earrings and necklace, no indigo, jasmine, tali or coin necklace. No painted text. Clear night sky upper right for the balloon.

Nagoji wears a hanging gold drop earring, clearly visible below the lobe. The author has ruled that it must be a small flush stud, enforced in selection. He is also drawn large and in sharp focus, not small and out of focus behind Varma as the script asks, and has no grey at the temples. Varma himself is good: profile against the sky, grey low knot, sacred thread, one hand open on the wet stone.
decisions.correction: Keep Varma exactly as drawn: profile against the night sky, grey low knot, sacred thread across his bare chest, plain white mundu, one hand lying open on the wet stone while the other loosens its grip. Push Nagoji much further back along the wall walk, about a third of Varma's height, soft-focus and blurred like a background figure, so Varma clearly dominates the panel. Nagoji keeps the white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain and Kerala topknot, with a touch of grey at the temples. His ear ornament is a tiny flush gold stud on the lobe with nothing hanging below it: no drop, ball, bead or pearl. Keep the upper sky plain and dark for the two balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor: at this small scale Nagoji's ear ornament reads as a tiny pale bead just under the lobe, not a flush gold stud. It is a few pixels wide, so retouch it to a flush gold stud if possible. Nagoji has no grey at the temples. Varma's mundu has a gold border rather than plain, which matches the rest of the page. Otherwise on beat: wide 3:1 strip, Varma's arm opening toward the dark kingdom, fort lamps on far hills, the pale road, the camp cookfires, two small figures on the wet wall walk, Nagoji with a clean-shaven chin and thick moustache in the white coat and red waistcoat. No painted text. Wide clear sky band across the top for the balloon and two captions.

Minor: the camera is inside the chapel looking out at Nagoji in the doorway, not outside looking in, so the cross hangs on the inside wall rather than above the outer door. The beat still reads: De Lannoy kneels at the front pew, Duarte stands at the altar with hands raised (no Roman collar tab, ink-stained fingers) and Nagoji waits outside by the doorpost. Nagoji is on model, with a curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, grey temples, topknot, red waistcoat and chain of office. The small brass altar crucifix and chalice are acceptable. The granite wall in the upper middle, between the door and Duarte, gives clear space for both captions.

Minor: De Lannoy's hair reads as pale ash-blond with only a little grey. He wears white breeches here but a mundu-like lower garment in 10.4. Otherwise clean: he has stepped out of the chapel and faces Nagoji, who stands at the doorpost with a curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, grey temple streak, topknot, chain of office and no turban. Sky in the upper left takes De Lannoy's balloon. The granite above the door, upper right, takes Nagoji's.

Setting and continuity break. De Lannoy is drawn back INSIDE the chapel beside the altar, and Duarte stands in the doorway with the outdoor dusk behind him. In 10.2 De Lannoy has already stepped outside, and in 10.4 he is outside at the doorframe. So this panel flips the geometry: it reads as De Lannoy back inside and Duarte leaving, not Duarte in the doorway behind De Lannoy. De Lannoy also dominates the foreground in a mundu and sash, while the panel's subject (the caption is about Duarte's eyes) is small and in the midground. Duarte himself is on model: grey-white curls, no collar tab, ink-stained clasped hands, small cross.
decisions.correction: Put the camera OUTSIDE the chapel in the evening forecourt, looking at the chapel's open doorway in local granite with a simple wooden cross above it, the same exterior and warm low light as the previous panel. Father Duarte is the focus, a mid-shot standing IN the open doorway, framed by the door, with the dim candlelit chapel interior (altar, front pew) behind him. Show his scholar's stoop, white-grey swept curly hair, and grey tired eyes looking out with quiet acceptance, not lowered. His callused, ink-stained hands are loosely clasped at his waist. He wears a plain black cassock with a plain black standing collar and a small cross on a thin chain, NO white collar tab. De Lannoy is OUTSIDE, in the near foreground at the left edge, in three-quarter back view: tall, pale grey hair tied with a black ribbon, worn white coat over a buff waistcoat, white breeches as in the previous panel. He has just stepped past the threshold, and Duarte stands behind him. Do NOT place De Lannoy inside the chapel or near the altar, and keep him smaller than Duarte in the frame. Leave the granite wall above the door and the sky at the upper left clear and low-detail for a caption and a speech balloon.

decisions.issues: Minor: De Lannoy wears a mundu-like white lower garment, as on his sheet, where 10.2 shows breeches. His hair reads as pale ash-blond with grey. Otherwise the beat is exact: his palm lies flat on the granite doorframe (a well-formed hand), his mouth is open in speech, and the fort walls rise behind him in evening light. The large sky in the upper left holds both balloons easily.

Minor: Nagoji's hair is all black, with none of the grey at the temples shown in 10.1 and 10.2. Otherwise on model: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin (texture shading only), small gold stud, topknot, red waistcoat, brass buttons and chain of office. The order is correct, left to right De Lannoy, Nagoji, Duarte, with the chapel door behind them and the fort wall in low evening light. Duarte (no collar tab) steps toward Nagoji with his ink-stained right hand lifting. Balloon space is tight at the upper left but ample in the sky at the upper right and over the chapel gable.

Strong composition and beat (Duarte's ink-stained, callused hand stopped between them, sleeve back from the wrist, Nagoji in white coat, red waistcoat, topknot, grey temples and a tiny flush gold stud, watching the hand). But Duarte's collar shows a white Roman-collar tab at its front notch (about x 0.77, y 0.37). It is visible even on the contact sheet, and it is the anachronism the script bans in every Duarte panel. With no lettering in this panel, nothing will cover it. Nagoji also has light stubble shading on the jaw.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition: the chapel doorway at evening with the altar, two lamps and the wooden cross behind; Nagoji at left in the white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain, hands behind his back, topknot with grey at the temples, tiny flush gold ear stud, looking down at the hand; Duarte at right, stooped, eyes lowered, his ink-stained right hand stopped in the air between them with the cassock sleeve fallen back from the wrist. Fix only the following. Duarte's cassock collar is a plain black standing collar closed all the way round the throat, black at its front opening, with no white tab, white notch or white linen showing anywhere at the neck. Nagoji's jaw and chin are smooth and clean-shaven, with no stubble shading.

decisions.issues: Wrong beat. Duarte's eyes are closed and his ink-stained fingers press against his own forehead, so he reads as crossing himself or nursing a headache in grief, not blessing Nagoji. He stands inside the chapel turned away from where Nagoji would be. The altar also carries a figured crucifix, which goes against the plain-altar setting used in the other panels.
decisions.correction: Show Duarte giving a blessing to another man, not crossing himself. Place Duarte in the right half of the frame, in the chapel doorway at evening, facing frame left toward Nagoji, who is just off-panel to the left. His eyes are open and rest on Nagoji with a calm, deliberate look. His callused, ink-stained right hand is raised in front of him at shoulder height, held away from his body, with the first two fingers extended together and the palm turned outward toward frame left, tracing the sign of the cross in the air toward Nagoji. The black cassock sleeve has fallen back from the wrist. The hand does not touch his own forehead, face or chest. His left hand hangs at his side. Use the same setting as the neighbouring panels: the stone chapel doorway in low warm evening light, with a plain altar under a white cloth, two brass lamps and a plain wooden cross on the wall behind. No figure on the cross and no crucifix on the altar. Keep his collar plain black and closed, with no white tab. Leave the upper-left area of plain stone wall or evening sky clear and low-detail for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: De Lannoy's hair is ash-blond with grey streaks rather than a fully pale grey, but this falls within the range of the page 10 panels. Otherwise clean: both men half-smiling; De Lannoy clean-shaven in a worn white coat over a buff waistcoat; Duarte white-haired, his black standing collar closed with no white tab, small cross, ink-stained fingers. The chapel interior matches 11.1. The rafters and the plaster wall above the cross leave room for both balloons.

Minor: De Lannoy's hair reads ash-blond rather than pale grey, darker than in 11.3. His expression is a little stern for 'Quiet'. Otherwise the beat is right: tall, clean-shaven, in a worn and smudged white coat, looking back through the open chapel door at the floor before the altar. There is no text. The plain plaster wall above the cross and the stone arch in the upper area give room for the long balloon.

Nagoji is off-model. His ear ornament is a gold ball hanging from the lobe, not the required tiny flush stud. His jaw and chin carry visible stubble. His hair falls in long loose curls around his shoulders with only a small bun, rather than the Kerala topknot, and shows no grey at the temples. The mood also reads as confrontation: De Lannoy grips Nagoji's arm with a hard frown and Nagoji glares back, which works against 'We are all servants now'. The composition, left-to-right order, chapel, fort wall and sky band are all good.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition: a wide evening strip with the stone chapel and its lit doorway at left, the fort wall and hill behind, and a clear band of evening sky across the upper part of the frame. Left to right: De Lannoy, Nagoji, Duarte, with De Lannoy's right hand gripping Nagoji's forearm. Fix Nagoji. His ear ornament is a tiny flush gold stud sitting on the lobe, with nothing hanging below it. His jaw and chin are smooth and clean-shaven with no stubble, and he keeps the thick curled moustache. His hair is gathered up into a Kerala topknot high on the crown, with only a few short curls at the nape, and shows first grey at the temples. Make the moment warm, not tense. The grip is a comradely clasp. De Lannoy looks earnest, with a faint steady smile. Nagoji listens with a softened face and turns toward him. Duarte stands beside them with a gentle, content look. Duarte keeps the plain black standing collar closed, with no white tab.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate) is otherwise strong: dusk star-fort rampart, storm over the sea on the right, Nagoji leaning on the parapet in the gold-bordered white mundu with a grey-streaked topknot, and a young, round-faced, clean-shaven officer in a white coat and red waistcoat beside him. The open sky is good for lettering. It fails on Nagoji's identity. His ear ornament is a round gold bead hanging below the lobe, which is the drop from the sheet and not the flush stud the author ruled on 2026-10-02. He also shows visible grey stubble across the chin and jaw, where the bible requires a clean-shaven chin outside captivity.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's ear ornament must be a tiny flush gold stud set directly ON the earlobe, no bigger than a lentil, with nothing hanging from it: no ball, bead, drop or ring below the lobe (the previous attempt copied the hanging gold drop from the reference sheet; do not). His chin, jaw and cheeks are smooth and fully clean-shaven, with no grey stubble or beard shadow; the only facial hair is the thick curled grey-and-black moustache. Keep everything else exactly as before: the dusk laterite rampart with the storm and rain far out over the sea on the right, Nagoji on the right of centre leaning both forearms on the parapet in the gold-bordered white mundu draped over one shoulder with his grey-streaked topknot, the young round-faced clean-shaven officer in a white coat and red waistcoat beside him on the left, and open sky across the top of the frame for lettering.

decisions.issues: Minor: the edges are sharp, not a soft faded memory bleed, so the bleed would have to come from the compositor. Two brass lamps sit at the table corners, off the map. The blue coastal marks read a little like small lakes. There is no lettering or pseudo-writing anywhere, and the colour regions (red, black, brown, blue marks, pale patches on the south-west coast, sea to the left) match the script.

Minor: the officer is in back three-quarter view, and his hair is tied at the back of the head rather than in a crown tuft. Nagoji has very faint shading on his chin, within tolerance. The ear stud is flush and correct, and the setting matches panel 1.

Minor: the masthead flags are plain red with no visible conch at this scale (there is no lettering on them). The musketeers' white coats read as long white tunics. Everything else matches: a volley drill with cross-belts, the red silver-conch standard, the shore battery, horsemen in the surf and lateen-sail coastal craft. The dark cloud band across the top is clear for both captions.

Minor: the officer looks somewhat older and heavier than twenty, and his hair is a back knot rather than a small crown tuft. He is still round-faced, has no moustache and wears the white coat. This is a reverse angle, so the sea sits on the left, consistent with the parapet side. Nagoji's ear stud is flush and his chin is essentially clean.

Duarte is drawn grey-haired as on his sheet rather than the script's 'dark-haired' younger Duarte; the bible base line (grey hair in his fifties, which is how he looks in Ch1) overrides the script, so this is acceptable. Nagoji's ear stud reads as a tiny gold bead rather than a perfectly flush stud (minor at print size). The memory treatment is a faded torn-paper edge with fairly warm colour rather than strong desaturation. Otherwise clean: captivity costume, loose black hair with no grey, curled moustache, clean chin, wrists bound by rope to the stool, ankle irons, barefoot; rope is a coiled hank on an iron ring, no noose; no Roman collar tab; no painted text. Open stone wall in the upper centre between the two heads holds the balloon and two captions.

Minor: no sandalwood line visible at Revathi's hairline; Nagoji's expression is a faint closed-mouth smile. Otherwise matches: Revathi in indigo and gold with a jasmine braid, grey threading, the tali on a yellow thread, flat-coin necklace and gold armlets, turning with a raised finger toward the running niece; Nagoji behind her with a topknot, grey at the temples, a cream mundu and shoulder cloth, a silver chain, no knife, curled moustache, clean chin and ear stud. Brass open-wick lamps, wet stone, rain at the eaves, soft faded memory edges. Caption space: the dark rainy sky and eaves at upper right and the wall above the heads at top centre.

Minor: Revathi's braid is still mostly black below a grey crown, and her face reads only moderately aged. Otherwise correct: the split is down the middle under one rain, Kochi on the left and Velinadu on the right. Elderly Savitri is in plain white among banana plants and herb beds, with only a thin chain and no indigo, jasmine or tali. Revathi is on the verandah in indigo and gold with jasmine, the bead/coin necklace, armlets and a sandalwood mark. Laughing children run through the wet corridor, and there are no children in the Kochi half. The top bands of both halves (sky and eaves) hold the place tags; the roof and sky at upper right hold the extra caption.

Minor: a faint shadow of stubble on the chin (reads clean-shaven at print size), loose curls fall behind the grey-streaked topknot, and braziers burn in the rain. Otherwise matches the beat: Nagoji alone on the star-fort rampart, face lifted to the rain with eyes closed, a gold-bordered white mundu over one shoulder, no coat or turban, curled moustache and a flush gold ear stud. Below him are forts, roads, fields, the shore battery and a grey surf. The flags are plain cloth, there is no painted text, and both hands are sound. The broad stormy sky across the top holds all five captions.
